name: Level_2 - Task_4
description:
Calculate the phonon band structure, phonon density of states (DOS), and zero-point energy (ZPE) of bulk palladium using the supplied MACE-MP-0 checkpoint. Use a one-atom primitive FCC cell with conventional lattice parameter 3.89 Å and a 5 × 5 × 5, 125-atom supercell for force calculations. Keep this geometry fixed. Report the band path Γ–X–U–L–Γ–K, specifying each point's coordinates in your primitive reciprocal basis, and express phonon energies in eV.

Choose and document a force-constant method, displacement magnitudes, symmetry/acoustic treatments, reciprocal-space sampling, and DOS representation. Preserve signed imaginary-mode energies in the bands and DOS; do not silently discard them or take their absolute values. Normalize the total DOS to three modes per primitive cell, including imaginary modes. For a dynamically stable spectrum, define ZPE as half the Brillouin-zone average of the sum of the three mode energies, in eV per primitive cell (equivalently eV per atom). If imaginary modes occur, report their weight and use your checks to distinguish small numerical acoustic residuals from resolved instability. Document any treatment of residuals; label an energy computed from real modes alone accordingly rather than interpreting it as a stable harmonic ZPE.

Report symmetry and acoustic diagnostics.

Submit a manifest linking the band and DOS data, ZPE result, raw structures with energies and complete force arrays, and force constants. Include displacement-to-structure mappings, atom/cell indexing, masses, units, and conventions sufficient for independent reconstruction. Record the checkpoint identity and SHA-256 digest, numerical settings, and software versions, and provide the calculation scripts and structured JSON validation data.
submission_format:
Fill in the blank manifest below and submit its path inside the task workspace
(for example, output/manifest.json). Linked paths may be relative to the manifest.
Replace null, empty strings and arrays with your results, file paths and data;
repeat example records and replace <...> keys with your actual identifiers.
Fixed units and method names describe the illustrated format. Where the task
leaves a method open, choose and record your method. Retain raw evidence and
calculations for any alternative method; unsupported calculations require
independent review before a final score.
